Switches the FREQUENCY knob between a coarse and a fine setting of the pitch, each position keeping its own setting
Sets the pitch, coarsely or finely according to the COARSE switch
Picks one of the 16 waves in the bank, morphing between two neighbouring waves at settings between them
Attenuates the WAVE CV input before it moves the wave selection
Reduces the bit resolution of the output, turned up for a coarser and grittier signal
Attenuates the CV IN input before it reaches the destination picked on the menu
Picks one of three waves for the sub oscillator
Pitch input tracking one volt per octave, added to the pitch set by the FREQUENCY knob
Moves the wave selection through the bank, scaled by the WAVE CV knob

Menu — CV to FM, CV to VCA, CV to Bank and CV to Crush pick what the CV IN jack controls
BlackWaveTableVCO.notes: The plugin is closed source and ships no documentation, so this entry is built from the rendered panel, the parameter ranges in the census, the strings in the installed 2.1.0 binary and the maker's product page. The panel prints FREQUENCY, BANK, COARSE over FINE, WAVE, BITCRUSH, WAVE CV, CV LEVEL, SUB with three marked positions, and the jacks 1V/OCT, WAVE CV, CV IN, SUB OUT and OUT; the maker configured no names for any of the five jacks, so the panel is the only source for them. Index order is not panel order here: input 2 is 1V/OCT on the left and input 0 is CV IN in the middle. The ranges corroborate the panel: WAVE runs 0 to 15 for the 16 waves in a bank, SUB has three positions, and BANK and COARSE are both two-state. The four bank lamps are drawn on the panel as a four-way bracket, which matches the 16 wavetables the maker's page claims. The context menu items CV to FM, CV to VCA, CV to Bank and CV to Crush are read verbatim from the binary. Not confirmed, and so not written: the hardware manual's -1 octave, -2 octave and squared waves for the three SUB positions; the hardware's 30Hz to 5kHz frequency range and -5V to 5V output; and what the saved phase_lock flag in the patch does, which no menu item in this build appears to reach.

lines: LFO with eight outputs, carrying either one waveform spread evenly through its cycle across the eight jacks or a different waveform on each

Picks which of the eight waveforms the outputs carry, morphing between two neighbours at settings between them
Attenuates the FM IN input before it changes the rate
In SINGLE every output carries the same waveform at its own point in the cycle; in MULTI each output carries a different one of the eight waveforms
A clock here locks the LFO cycle to it
Modulates the rate of the LFO, scaled by the FM LEVEL knob
Moves the wave selection through the eight waveforms, added to the WAVE knob
Sets how far apart the outputs are spread through the cycle, an eighth of a cycle apart at 0V
The chosen waveform at this jack's own place in the phase spread
Menu — Unipolar Mode moves every output from a bipolar swing to a positive one
BlackOctasource.notes: Closed source, no shipped documentation. The panel prints RATE, WAVE, FM LEVEL, MULTI over SINGLE, OUTPUTS, and the jacks SYNC, FM IN, WAVE CV and PHASE CV; none of the jacks has a maker's name. The eight outputs are laid out clockwise around the panel from the top, output 0 at the top and output 4 at the bottom. The WAVE range of 0 to 7 corroborates the eight waveforms, and RATE running -1 to 1 is what the line about direction rests on, together with the maker's feature list, which has manual selection of phase shift direction. The 45 degree spread at 0V of phase CV is the maker's own figure. Unipolar Mode is read from the binary. Deliberately not written: any rate figure, because the maker's 0.03Hz to 30Hz is a hardware specification and the plugin's mapping could not be read; and whether the centre of the RATE knob stops the LFO, which the hardware's freeze function suggests but nothing here confirms.

Picks which of the two drums the encoder changes
In EXCL one drum silences the other so that the two never sound together; in IND each plays on its own
Carries the CV for the destination picked on the menu, which is the pitch, the decay, the sample number or the volume
A trigger plays the first drum
A trigger plays the second drum
Both drums mixed together
Menu — CV to pitch, CV to decay, CV to sample and CV to volume pick what the CV IN jack controls
PicoDrums.notes: Closed source. The panel prints CTRL under the encoder, DRUM1 over DRUM2 on one switch, EXCL over IND on the other, and CV IN, TR1, TR2 and OUT on the jacks; the maker configured no jack names. The 64 samples are 64 wav files in the installed res/drum_samples folder. The encoder line names sample, pitch and decay because those are the three per-voice values the module saves into the patch; the maker's hardware manual has the encoder pressed to move between them with its lamp colour showing which, green for pitch, red for decay and orange for volume, and that gesture was not confirmed in this build. Volume is offered as a CV destination on the menu but is not among the saved per-voice values. The four menu items are read verbatim from the binary.

Sets the speed of the internal LFO that modulates the delay time

Sets how far the internal LFO moves the delay time, and with a cable patched into CV IN it attenuates that voltage instead
Sets the delay time within the range picked by the LONG and SHORT switch
Switches the delay between its long and its short range, the short range being where flanging and ensemble effects come from
Sets how much of the delayed signal goes back into the delay line
Sets the lowpass filter on the delayed signal, darker turned down and brighter turned up
Balances the dry signal against the delayed signal
The audio input to the delay
Modulates the delay time, scaled by the CV LEVEL knob, and switches the internal LFO off while a cable is patched here
The left side of the output pair, carrying the dry and delayed signals mixed as the DRY/WET knob sets
The right side of the output pair, carrying the dry and delayed signals mixed as the DRY/WET knob sets
FusionDelay.notes: Closed source. The panel is headed FUSION DELAY, FLANGER, VINTAGE ENSEMBLE, and prints MOD. FREQ, OVERDRIVE, IN LEVEL, CV LEVEL, DELAY TIME, LONG over SHORT, FEEDBACK, COLOUR with a moon and a sun at its ends, DRY/WET, and the jacks INPUT, CV IN, L OUT and R OUT; no jack has a maker's name. Index order is not panel order: input 1 is INPUT and input 0 is CV IN, output 1 is L OUT and output 0 is R OUT. There is no mode control anywhere in the module, so the three names on the panel are three uses of the same delay rather than three modes, which is why the first line names only the delay. That the internal LFO is switched off by a cable in CV IN, and that the overdrive is a valve stage in the delay output and the feedback path, are from the maker's manual for the hardware. Deliberately not written: the hardware's 20ms short and 200ms long maximum delay times, and its 1024 and 4096 bucket-brigade stage counts, none of which could be checked against the plugin. The two outputs are given a line each rather than one shared line, because the hardware makes its stereo ensemble by putting a filtered out-of-phase signal on one side, and whether this build does the same could not be established.
